tools.description:
Retrieve reference leads using lexical overlap with authored applicability text.

This existing heuristic does not decide whether a target satisfies preconditions.
It does not reason about negation, quantifiers, conjunctions, or capability access.
Even a high score is text relevance only. Inspect source scope and limitations;
defeated_by commentary is not a general immunity theorem. The historical
capability_gates_met field means lexical overlap, not established capability.
Only records with reviewed applicability text are searched. Empty results do
not establish that no relevant result exists.
tools.name: attack-catalog-mcp_find_applicable_attacks

tools.description:
Return one attack by its stable catalog ID, with both layers.

`normalized` carries the classification and review states; `legacy` preserves
the published record's preserved non-identity fields. Historical aliases are returned
as references but do not resolve as lookup IDs. Both
are returned so any classification can be audited against the value it came from.
tools.name: attack-catalog-mcp_get_attack

tools.description: Describe the loaded snapshot, refresh limits, registry pin, and reading-guide index.
tools.name: attack-catalog-mcp_get_catalog_info

tools.description: Explain the filter semantics: rollup, result-level matching, and absence handling.
tools.name: attack-catalog-mcp_get_filter_contract

tools.description: Return source metadata and its content digest; this does not retrieve or verify a paper.
tools.name: attack-catalog-mcp_get_source

tools.description:
List subject references for an exact runtime skill ID, in canonical ID order.

Links are reading relevance only, never mandatory invocations or applicability evidence.
Editorial additions carry their authorship and limited evidence scope. Pagination uses
offsets within the returned snapshot digest; stop or restart if that digest changes.
tools.name: attack-catalog-mcp_list_attacks_for_skill

tools.description:
List dimensions, or the terms and hierarchy of one dimension.

Call this before guessing a filter value. Terms are data and may grow between releases.
tools.name: attack-catalog-mcp_list_taxonomy

tools.description:
Search the loaded promoted catalog snapshot using NORMALIZED filters.

Hierarchical dimensions roll up: outcome=key_recovery returns private-key, symmetric-key,
session-key, shared-secret and partial recoveries. Every result reports matched_by, naming
the dimension and the exact term that produced the match, and for result-level dimensions
which result variant matched.

Two distinctions that change answers:
  * outcome is what a record DEMONSTRATES. An attack on a hardness assumption carries
    outcome=assumption_solver and is NOT returned by outcome=key_recovery; ask
    potential_scheme_impact=key_recovery for what it would yield once instantiated.
  * shared_secret_recovery is not session_key_recovery. A derivation step may stand
    between the raw shared secret and the session key.

Use list_taxonomy first if unsure which terms exist; unknown terms are rejected rather
than silently ignored.
tools.name: attack-catalog-mcp_search_attacks

tools.description:
NON-SEMANTIC. Match one literal legacy string exactly.

This exists for debugging and export parity ONLY. It matches a single string and makes no
completeness claim: legacy `result_type` has 65 distinct free-text values, so
field='result_type', value='key recovery' returns 36 records while the semantic filter
outcome=key_recovery returns 116.

If you are answering a question about attacks, use search_attacks instead. Reaching for
this tool for a semantic question produces a wrong answer that looks right.
tools.name: attack-catalog-mcp_search_by_legacy_value_exact
